overview: The Pagan Kingdom was the first unified Burmese state, famous for the thousands of Buddhist temples and pagodas built on the plains of Bagan. Theravada Buddhism became firmly established and Burmese culture was codified under royal patronage.

items.text: Over 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas survive at Bagan from an original 10,000.
The Ananda Temple exemplifies Mon-influenced Burmese architecture with gilded spires.
Burmese script developed from Mon writing, enabling a national literature.
King Anawrahta converts to Theravada Buddhism and promotes it as the state religion.
The Tipitaka scriptures brought from Sri Lanka established orthodox Buddhist learning.
Bagan's temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Theravada Buddhism became and remains Burma's dominant religion.

fall.text: The kingdom collapsed following Mongol invasions and internal fragmentation.
